text: General waste (red or dark-green lid) bins are collected weekly in the City of Melbourne. Recycling (yellow lid) bins are collected fortnightly, except for low-rise multi-unit properties with a communal food and garden organics service, which get weekly recycling collection.
Food and garden waste (lime-green lid) bins are collected weekly in the City of Melbourne.
Recycling and general waste bins are collected on all public holidays except Good Friday and Christmas Day, where collections shift to the following Saturday.

City of Melbourne residents are entitled to one free hard waste collection, or one cubic metre, per financial year. Bookings are essential and dates are made available two months in advance. Commercial or retail addresses are not entitled to a hard waste collection.

On the day before hard waste collection, items must be placed on the kerbside or in an accessible location. Under no circumstances will City of Melbourne enter a private property boundary to collect items.

All bins in the City of Melbourne must be stored within a property or premises and must not be permanently stored in a street, laneway, footpath, or collection site outside of collection hours. Bins placed in the public space for collection must be locked.

A permit is required for each bin or skip placed on a road or City of Melbourne-owned land, if bins cannot be collected from within the property. Skip bin street placement permits are separate from ongoing bin collection.

The Waste Charge on a City of Melbourne rates notice is calculated using the Capital Improved Value (CIV) of the property, the same calculation method used for general rates. It is audited annually by the Essential Services Commission and does not generate additional revenue for the council.

Residential ratepayers who are ineligible to access City of Melbourne's waste services (for example due to using a private waste service in a high-rise building) may not be charged the Waste Charge, though eligibility varies by property type.

City of Melbourne rates can be viewed and managed via the eRates online portal. Ratepayers register using their name and assessment number exactly as shown on their rates notice, and can choose to receive notices via email instead of post.

If applying for a planning permit for a development in the City of Melbourne, applicants may be required to submit a Waste Management Plan outlining how the development will manage its waste and recycling needs.
The City of Melbourne operates parking permits that residents can apply for, renew, and pay for online, alongside options to report illegal or abandoned parking and view or dispute a parking fine.

Melbourne does not have one city-wide hard rubbish collection system. Local government areas across greater Melbourne, including the City of Melbourne, each set their own waste policies, booking processes, accepted items, and collection allowances, so rules can differ significantly between neighbouring council areas.

Companies collecting commercial waste from businesses in the City of Melbourne's central city area must hold a waste collector permit for each vehicle used, as part of council efforts to keep the central city clean and reduce late-night collection disturbance.
Street maintenance issues, including problems with public bins, dumped waste, or graffiti, can be reported to the City of Melbourne through their online 'Pay, report, request' service portal.
